metadata.title: ICILS 2023. Technischer Bericht
metadata.venue: Institut des Bundes für Qualitätssicherung im österreichischen Schulwesen (IQS)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICILS 2023 uses a two-stage school-and-class sampling design with additional teacher sampling within selected schools, and the report describes explicit stratification and PPS (probability proportional to size) selection of schools. In Austria, schools were selected using PPS based on the number of eighth-graders (MOS), with explicit strata defined by school type, an index of social factors, and urbanisation, plus implicit stratification by Bundesland and MOS. The report also documents exclusion rules (e.g., special education schools, very small schools, and foreign-language schools) and participation thresholds that affect the effective coverage of the target population. Although the technical report states that IEA performs weighting and scaling after data submission, it does not specify the exact student weight variable names or replicate-weight method in the provided text; therefore, analysts should follow the IEA ICILS technical documentation for the correct weight variables and variance estimation approach.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a technical report describing study frameworks, sampling, administration, and scoring procedures rather than estimating student-level predictive models with a PV-based cognitive outcome. Plausible Values handling is therefore not applicable in the sense of PV-based achievement modeling, because the provided text focuses on instrument development, sampling/participation, and scoring logistics. Missing-data handling is not reported here because the report does not present an empirical modeling analysis with an explicit missing-data protocol for a statistical outcome.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Target population comprises students in the eighth grade (ISCED Level 1 equivalent) with the international age criterion satisfied at the population level; in Austria this means all students taught in grade 8 regardless of individual age. Schools were excluded at the sampling frame level: special education schools, very small schools (<3 students in grade 8), and foreign-language schools that teach only classes in a language other than German. Within selected schools, one or two classes were randomly sampled using WinW3S, and all students in those classes were targeted, except students excluded via international exclusion codes for physical/mental impairment or insufficient language proficiency. For the main test, schools were treated as non-participating if in at least one selected class fewer than half of students participated; students were considered participating if they completed at least one test task. Participation thresholds were also applied for teacher questionnaires (school non-participation if <50% of selected teachers completed the teacher questionnaire), and for school-level questionnaires a school counted as participating if at least one of the two school/IT-coordinator questionnaires was completed. The realized main-test student sample in Austria is 3,448 tested students after exclusions and non-participation.

data.outcome_summary: ICILS 2023 is an international, computer-based assessment of computer and information literacy (CIL) for students in grade 8, with an optional computational thinking (CT) domain. The technical report details the study’s framework (CIL and CT constructs), the development and translation/verification of test instruments and questionnaires, and the Austrian implementation timeline (field test in 2022; main test in May–June 2023). Sampling in Austria follows a two-stage design: schools are selected with PPS using the number of eighth-graders (MOS), then one or two classes are randomly selected within each school; all students in selected classes are targeted, with additional random teacher sampling. The report documents exclusion criteria at school level (special education, very small schools, foreign-language schools) and participation rules (e.g., student participation thresholds and teacher questionnaire completion thresholds). Scoring is described as automated for most tasks via Assessment Master™ and manual expert scoring for constructed/large tasks, including double marking for about 20% of responses and a minimum agreement criterion of 70%.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a technical report focused on assessment design, sampling, administration, and scoring quality assurance rather than an empirical predictive/causal analysis. Consequently, there are no ML models, target variables, or performance metrics to extract, and the report does not provide PV-based modeling results or an explicit missing-data handling protocol for statistical estimation. The sparse ML-related fields are therefore expected by design.
